$schema_note: NEX Stairplan MASTER MATERIAL LIBRARY — the single source of truth for every material used across the platform. Components in staircase-components.json reference materials BY MAT ID only (e.g. HR-014.material_id = 'MAT-002'). Change MAT-002 once here, every staircase in Stairplan automatically inherits the improvement. Do not duplicate material properties anywhere else.
canonical_id_rule: Every material has ONE canonical MAT-ID. Downstream systems (components, pricing, rendering, marketing) reference by ID only. Never duplicate material properties.
build_order_note: Per Philip (2026-07-25): MATERIALS FIRST, then handrails, newels, balusters, glass, strings, treads, landings, metal, staircase presets. Rationale — every component references materials, so perfecting materials first perfects every downstream component automatically.

reference_asset_checklist.description: Per material, the standard set of reference images Philip generates and Claude catalogues. Populate the marketing_images object on each material as URLs become available.

assets.purpose: Marketing banner + Real House Mode reference

materials.name: European Oak

appearance.colour: Warm golden-brown with prominent medullary rays
appearance.grain: Straight, sometimes wavy or figured on quarter-sawn boards
appearance.variation: Notable — every board slightly different; darker heartwood streaks common

materials.nex_description: European Oak is the UK default premium staircase timber — warm, characterful, wildly versatile. Works in a Georgian townhouse or a modern new-build without fighting either. Ages beautifully; a well-made European oak staircase reads as heirloom joinery after 30 years. Pairs equally with turned traditional detail or slim contemporary glass.

materials.name: American White Oak

appearance.colour: Light golden brown with warm honey tones
appearance.variation: Natural — cleaner and paler than European oak, less prominent medullary rays

materials.nex_description: American White Oak is one of the world's most popular staircase timbers — prized for strength, stability, and a warm natural appearance. Pale honey tones and clean straight grain make it a favourite for modern and Scandinavian interiors. Pairs exceptionally well with frameless glass balustrades and black metal details.

materials.name: American Walnut

appearance.colour: Rich chocolate-brown with darker striping and occasional purple undertones
appearance.grain: Straight to wavy, often with distinctive figuring
appearance.variation: Substantial — flame figure and burl patches common in premium grades

materials.nex_description: American Walnut is one of the finest luxury staircase timbers available. Deep chocolate tones with darker striping, and it deepens and enriches as it ages — a walnut staircase becomes MORE beautiful over 20 years, not less. The go-to for statement staircases in premium homes.

materials.name: European Ash

appearance.colour: Pale cream to light blonde, sometimes with darker brown streaks in the heartwood
appearance.grain: Straight, prominent open grain — similar structure to oak

materials.nex_description: Ash is the pale, bright hardwood — nearly as hard as oak but visually much lighter. Perfect for modern Scandi and coastal interiors where you want the strength of a hardwood without the golden warmth of oak. Takes stains beautifully so it doubles as a base for coloured finishes.

materials.name: Scandinavian Pine (Redwood)

appearance.colour: Pale yellow to light amber, darkens to warm honey with age
appearance.variation: High — knot patterns vary widely; grade determines how much character is visible

materials.nex_description: Scandinavian Pine is the UK default painted-staircase timber — economical, stable, works brilliantly under paint. For a natural clear-finished staircase pine is softer than the hardwoods (marks more easily) but for painted cottage/coastal/Scandi looks it's genuinely the best choice: takes primer + paint smoother than any hardwood.

materials.name: Sapele

appearance.colour: Medium to dark reddish-brown

materials.nex_description: Sapele is often specified where genuine mahogany would once have been — reddish-brown African hardwood with distinctive interlocked ribbon-figured grain. Dense, durable, takes a beautiful French-polished finish. Widely used on quality traditional and Victorian-style staircase work.

materials.name: Genuine Mahogany

appearance.colour: Rich reddish-brown, deepening with age

materials.nex_description: Genuine mahogany (Swietenia species) is CITES-restricted so genuine stock is rare and premium. The classic Georgian and Victorian staircase timber — deep reddish-brown, tight straight grain, polishes to a mirror finish. Most modern 'mahogany' staircases now use sapele or sipo (see MAT-006).

materials.name: American Cherry

appearance.colour: Warm pinkish-brown, deepening to rich red-brown with UV exposure

materials.nex_description: American cherry starts as a warm pinkish-brown and deepens to a rich red-brown over the first year or two — the ageing patina is one of the reasons people choose it. Silky-smooth, polishes beautifully, sits perfectly in traditional and Arts-and-Crafts interiors.

materials.name: Hard Maple

appearance.colour: Very pale, near-white to light cream
appearance.grain: Fine, straight, sometimes birds-eye or curly figured

materials.nex_description: Hard maple is one of the palest hardwoods and one of the hardest — the traditional timber for basketball courts and bowling alleys. Very fine smooth grain, near-white colour, takes a mirror clear finish. Can yellow slightly under UV over decades, so best in interiors with controlled daylight.

materials.name: European Beech

appearance.colour: Pale cream to pinkish-white

materials.nex_description: European beech is pale, fine-grained and takes stains beautifully — often chosen where the customer wants a clean minimal look. Moves more than oak with humidity so needs good moisture control in the workshop.

materials.name: Hemlock

appearance.colour: Pale reddish-brown

materials.nex_description: Hemlock is a pale straight-grained softwood used as an alternative to pine for painted staircases — cleaner grain, less pronounced knots.

materials.name: Douglas Fir

appearance.colour: Warm reddish-orange with darker growth rings
appearance.grain: Straight, strong figure from prominent growth rings

materials.nex_description: Douglas Fir gives you a warm reddish softwood with strong growth-ring figure — harder than pine, works in structural and visible components. Popular in industrial-loft and farmhouse conversions where the exposed grain becomes a design feature.

materials.name: Accoya (modified softwood)
materials.origin: New Zealand pine, modified in the Netherlands

appearance.colour: Pale honey similar to pine
appearance.grain: Straight, similar to base pine but stabilised

materials.nex_description: Accoya is chemically-modified radiata pine — the modification massively increases dimensional stability and rot resistance. Overkill for standard interior staircases but ideal where the flight transitions to exterior use or sits in high-humidity conditions.

materials.name: MDF Paint Grade

appearance.colour: Uniform brown (invisible under paint)

materials.nex_description: MDF is the engineered-board choice for painted staircase carcass work — cost-effective, no grain to show through paint, machines cleanly. Use for risers, painted strings, cover slips. Never use MDF on treads or structural elements — it's not rated for foot traffic.

materials.name: White Primed Timber

appearance.colour: Factory-primed white ready for final coat
appearance.grain: Subtle timber grain visible under primer

materials.nex_description: Softwood delivered from the factory already primed white, saving the finisher a prep coat. Ideal for full-painted staircases — cottage, coastal, Scandi and any painted-cottage-style project. Combine with hardwood treads for the classic 'oak treads + painted string' combination.

materials.name: Satin Black Powder-Coated Steel
materials.origin: UK / European steel mills, powder-coated at fabrication

appearance.colour: Deep matt-satin black

materials.nex_description: Satin black powder-coated mild steel is the modern-industrial staircase workhorse — used for central spines, slim balusters, cable-balustrade posts, glass fixings, floating-staircase brackets. Powder-coating gives a durable factory-cured finish that resists chips and scuffs far better than wet paint.

materials.name: Brushed Stainless Steel
materials.origin: UK / European steel mills, brushed at fabrication

appearance.colour: Silver-grey with parallel brush lines

materials.nex_description: Brushed stainless steel is where you want metal that doesn't rust and doesn't shout — the natural pairing for frameless glass balustrades (point fixings, spider clamps, channels) and cable balustrading. Marine-grade (316) recommended in coastal properties.

materials.name: Toughened Clear Glass

appearance.colour: Clear with subtle green edge tint (from iron content)

materials.nex_description: Standard toughened safety glass — 10mm minimum on domestic balustrade panels. Shatters into small blunt cubes rather than shards. Clear glass has a subtle green edge tint from the iron content — if this bothers you, upgrade to Low-Iron (MAT-019).

materials.name: Low-Iron Glass

appearance.colour: Crystal-clear, no green edge tint

materials.nex_description: Low-iron (also called Optiwhite or ultra-clear) glass is the premium spec — reduced iron content removes the green tint you see on standard toughened glass edges. Worth the upgrade on any 12mm+ balustrade panel where the edge is visible.

materials.name: Bronze-Tinted Glass

appearance.colour: Warm bronze tint through the whole panel

materials.nex_description: Bronze-tinted toughened glass — warm through-tint for a richer alternative to grey smoked glass. Pairs beautifully with brass fittings and walnut/mahogany timber. Adds warmth to a modern staircase that clear glass makes feel cold.

materials.name: Smoked Grey Glass

appearance.colour: Grey tint through the whole panel

materials.nex_description: Smoked grey toughened glass — through-tint for privacy and drama. Pairs perfectly with black powder-coated steel and darker timber. Adds mood to a modern industrial staircase. Shows cleaning streaks more visibly than clear — factor into maintenance decision.

tng_sheeting.reference_notes: Product-shot 3-quarter view of an oak T&G plank. Warm honey colour, chamfered visible edges, tongue-and-groove joint visible. Use ONLY this image for T&G references across brain, catalogue, marketing. Not for 3D texture tiling (perspective shot).
tng_sheeting.species: Oak (species interchangeable — walnut, ash, pine also available)
tng_sheeting.install_technique: HIDDEN NAILING (through tongue side, next plank groove covers pin hole)
tng_sheeting.edge_trim: 25mm angle bead on both outer edges — covers raw sheeting edges + outer staircase side
tng_sheeting.underlying_battens: 2"×2" (50×50mm) rough drywood, fixed to inner back of staircase
